doc.title: Vincent Pelote interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 25, 2017

title: Blindfold test: Lunceford's 'Rhythm Is Our Business'
summary: He identifies Lunceford, praises its cleanness and the recorded bass, contrasting Ellington and Lunceford with Henderson.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Yeah. All right. How about this one?
Oh yeah, um, I don’t know what take, but it’s Jimmie Lunceford Orchestra, “Rhythm is our Business.” But there are two takes. I can’t tell you which one.
Phil Schaap could tell you, but I can’t.
Yeah. Phil Schaap could tell you easily, but I can’t. Oh I love that band. They were so clean. I mean it’s just like wow.
They really captured the string bass.

Yes. Also, leaders were smart enough to push that bass up front. And Ellington does the same thing. You can always hear the bass on an Ellington recording, and the same thing with Lunceford. Fletcher, not so much. Fletcher wasn’t really that hip with the recording thing. But Ellington was and so was Lunceford. And their recordings were wonderful. But I just always marvel at the clean, at how clean that band was. I mean —
And apparently a lot of showmanship too.
Yes, exactly, exactly, with the horns going up and tossing the hats up and stuff. That’s great stuff man.
